units.function: Filesystem tests for adjacent .env storage of the shared Agent JWT Secret and preservation-aware updates of CLI-managed environment entries.
units.dependencyDirection: Calls production CLI env helpers and doctor check against temporary filesystem paths; it does not invoke token signing/verification or server identity services.
units.keyDataModels: PAPERCLIP_AGENT_JWT_SECRET, config-adjacent .env file, managed versus operator-owned environment entries and newline/quoting format.
units.lifecycle: Creates/loads a Secret, checks presence, merges managed values while preserving operator content, and avoids replacing an unchanged file.
units.testAssessment: Focused Vitest passed 6/6. Preservation and dotenv round-trip cases are valuable, but new/rewrite permissions, atomicity, symlinks, concurrent writers, entropy, rotation/revocation and JWT claims are absent; temporary Secret fixtures are not cleaned up.
units.designRationale: Keep local/self-hosted configuration upgrades from overwriting operator-managed environment content while ensuring a signing Secret exists.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS self-hosted deployment needs non-destructive config evolution and secure identity key lifecycle across upgrades.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the byte-preservation, quoting and no-op-write cases for a dedicated config merger. Do not adopt a single adjacent shared Secret as the identity model; use a rotatable key provider with issuer/audience/scope/expiry/revocation contracts and permission, symlink, atomic-write and cleanup tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: A shared signing Secret presence check does not prove which identity issued a token, its audience or authority, and cannot supply the independent product-token and accountable-human semantics required by Company OS.
evidence: 2026-08-18 focused Vitest: 6 passed via existing local binary
